operations.gives: The magnetic field at a place and time
The decimal year for a date

fields.latitudeInDegrees: −90 to 90, geodetic on WGS84, north positive
fields.longitudeInDegrees: −180 to 360, east positive. NOAA's own test values use 240.
fields.decimalYear: The year plus the days before the date over the days in its year, so 1 January is a whole year. The field operation takes 2025.0 to 2030.0 and refuses anything else as outOfRange.
fields.date: A calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. One that doesn't exist, like 2027-02-29, is invalidInput.
fields.magneticDeclinationInDegrees: D, the angle from true north to magnetic north, east positive, −180 to 180
fields.inclinationInDegrees: I, the field's dip below the horizontal, down positive
fields.gridVariationInDegrees: GV, magnetic north measured from polar stereographic grid north, −180 to 180: D minus longitude at 55° N and above, D plus longitude at 55° S and below. null between.
fields.blackout: none, caution (H under 6000 nT) or unreliable (H under 2000 nT), NOAA's blackout zones around the magnetic poles

cases.note: NOAA's Table 6. Grid variation equals declination on the prime meridian.
At the equator grid variation is null: NOAA prints NaN.
Longitude 240 is −120: grid variation is declination plus longitude, wrapped to −180 to 180.
Near the north magnetic pole: horizontal intensity under 2000 nT, blackout unreliable, declination still given.
Horizontal intensity under 6000 nT: blackout caution.
The geographic north pole: longitude is undefined, so NOAA takes the limit along longitude 0. Blackout unreliable.
The geographic south pole, along longitude 0.
2030.0, the model's last instant: still computed.
Exactly 55° N, where grid variation starts: declination minus longitude.
The last day of a leap year: 2028 + 365/366.
Before the model's first instant: outOfRange, as NOAA's software refuses it.
After the model's last instant: outOfRange.
